newsitem.title: JAPAN: BankAmerica cuts Tokyo jobs but looks to expand.
newsitem.headline: BankAmerica cuts Tokyo jobs but looks to expand.

text.p: BankAmerica Corp said on Monday it will cut 50 percent of its current 200 jobs in Tokyo but added it will also look to expand here in the future as deregulation of the financial industry unfolds.

Arun Duggal, general manager of the bank's Japan operations, told Reuters the Tokyo branch of the U.S. bank will eliminate the jobs, mainly back-office jobs to be moved to Hong Kong, as part of a reorganisation.
A specific timetable for the cuts has not been decided.
Meanwhile, the bank plans to establish a securities arm in Japan in 1997, after receiving approval from the Finance Ministry, he said.

"The Japanese capital market is likely to offer attractive opportunities once deregulation as outlined by Prime Minister (Ryutaro) Hashimoto begins," he said. "It is a very exciting and timely shift for us."
Duggal also said no decision had been made on the size of a new bond market unit to be established.
The bank said in a statement it is looking to to strengthen its role in Tokyo's derivatives, securities, structured export finance and securitisation business.
It said the traditional bank business appears to have limited growth and profit opportunities for the bank in Japan.
